{{Short description|Loop integral parametrization}} 
{{more citations needed|date=July 2022}}
'''Schwinger parametrization''' is a technique for evaluating [[loop integral]]s which arise from [[Feynman diagram]]s with one or more loops. It is named after [[Julian Schwinger]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schwinger |first=Julian |date=1951-06-01 |title=On Gauge Invariance and Vacuum Polarization |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.82.664 |journal=Physical Review |volume=82 |issue=5 |pages=664–679 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.82.664|url-access=subscription }}</ref> who introduced the method in 1951 for [[quantum electrodynamics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kim |first=U-Rae |last2=Cho |first2=Sungwoong |last3=Lee |first3=Jungil |date=2023-06-01 |title=The art of Schwinger and Feynman parametrizations |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s40042-023-00764-3 |journal=Journal of the Korean Physical Society |language=en |volume=82 |issue=11 |pages=1023–1039 |doi=10.1007/s40042-023-00764-3 |issn=1976-8524|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Description ==
Using the observation that

:<math>\frac{1}{A^n}=\frac{1}{(n-1)!}\int^\infty_0 du \, u^{n-1}e^{-uA},</math>

one may simplify the integral:

:<math>\int \frac{dp}{A(p)^n}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(n)}\int dp \int^\infty_0 du \, u^{n-1}e^{-uA(p)}=\frac{1}{\Gamma(n)}\int^\infty_0 du \, u^{n-1} \int dp \, e^{-uA(p)},</math>

for <math display="inline">\mathrm{Re}(n)>0</math>.

=== Alternative parametrization ===
Another version of Schwinger parametrization is:

:<math>\frac{i}{A+i\epsilon}=\int^\infty_0 du \, e^{iu(A+i\epsilon)},</math>

which is convergent as long as <math>\epsilon >0</math> and <math>A \in \mathbb R</math>.<ref>{{cite book|first=M. D.|last=Schwartz|title=Quantum Field Theory and the Standard Model|publisher=Cambridge University Press|date=2014|chapter=33|edition=9|page=705|isbn=9781107034730}}</ref> It is easy to generalize this identity to n denominators.
